findings.criterion: §6.2 conflict-gate fixture corpus — implementation has 2 fixtures vs ~12 in RULE-001 spec
findings.finding: RULE-001 §6.2 enumerates 12 fixture scenarios (8 allow + 4 deny). The implementation provides 1 allow fixture and 1 deny fixture, following the SCP-R-001/002 minimal-smoke-test pattern. The DISPATCH-NOTE explicitly documents this decision: exhaustive coverage lives in the 19-case Conftest test suite (policies/tests/scp_r_004_test.rego); the conflict-gate fixtures are engine-agreement smoke tests, not exhaustive corpus. This is the same posture as SCP-R-001 and SCP-R-002. However, the spec (RULE-001 §6.2) states the full list as a 'Phase-2 deliverable' without explicitly calling any items optional. The implementation chose a reasonable subset but the gap between §6.2's stated 12 fixtures and the 2 landed fixtures is not formally acknowledged in the DISPATCH-NOTE scope table (the scope table mentions '1 allow + 1 deny, matching SCP-R-001/002 pattern' — adequate framing but not a verbatim §6.2 acknowledgement).
findings.impact: Low. No engine-agreement gap surfaces from the missing fixtures; the Conftest test suite covers every §6.2 scenario. The gap is documentational — future reviewers reading §6.2 against the fixture tree will find only 2 of 12 items and have to cross-reference the DISPATCH-NOTE to understand the scope decision.
findings.remediation: File TF-020P-002: 'Expand conflict-gate fixture corpus to match RULE-001 §6.2 verbatim (remaining 10 fixtures: empty-array allow, github-pr-url allow, non-github-url allow, decision-log-url allow, multi-waiver-all-with-urls allow, reason-absent allow, reason-empty-string allow, bare-domain deny, multi-waiver-mixed deny, text-mentioning-url deny) — or amend RULE-001 §6.2 text to mark the minimal-smoke-test pattern as the canonical implementation intent for v1.1.0, deferring exhaustive corpus to v1.2+.' No inline fix needed; MIN severity means this does not block APPROVED verdict.

findings.criterion: Renovate preset — does v1.1.0 require a renovate/v1.1.0 preset tag?
findings.finding: The renovate.json self-dogfood pin points to 'renovate/v1.0.0'. The Renovate preset (renovate/default.json) governs HOW Renovate bumps adopter wrapper pins; it does not track the workflow tag series. The VERSIONING.md notes the Renovate preset is on an independent tag series ('renovate/v*'). The preset content (renovate/default.json) is unchanged in this slice — only the workflow versioning changes with v1.1.0. The renovate/v1.0.0 tag correctly continues to describe the preset shape. No new renovate/v1.x.0 preset cut is required unless the preset content itself changes. The release notes acknowledge this ('the Renovate preset ... remains stable') implicitly via VERSIONING.md. This is acceptable as-is.
findings.impact: None. The preset version series is independent of the workflow version series per VERSIONING.md.
findings.remediation: No action. The DISPATCH-NOTE scope table already addresses this under 'What does NOT count as breaking'.

rule_001_s9_deliverables.notes: RULE-001 §9 names these Phase-2 deliverables: (1) MINOR bump v1.0.1 → v1.1.0 — DONE (version-manifest.json). (2) Release notes naming SCP-R-004 + adopter response options + 90-day window — DONE (docs/releases/v1.1.0.md). (3) ADOPT-001 maintenance — new §12.7.14 with three response options (gradual amendment / rule-config disable / bulk cleanup) — DONE. (4) Estate-wide coordination D-NNN — RULE-001 §7 says this is a Phase-2 deliverable filed as part of the v1.1.0 cut; the release notes note 'No new D-NNN in this release' on grounds that SCP-R-004 is same-domain as SCP-R-002. This is consistent with README.md §3 Merge (same-domain rules do not require a merge-time D-NNN). The §7 estate coordination D-NNN described in RULE-001 is the coordination notice to adopters re: 90-day transition; this function is served by ADOPT-001 §12.7.14 + release notes. No standalone D-NNN row is strictly required by VERSIONING.md or README.md for a same-domain warn-baseline rule. Acceptable.

warn_baseline_bypass_surface.analysis: The WARN_BASELINE_RULES set is an allow-list. SCP-R-001/002/003 remain in the deny-baseline branch unchanged. SCP-R-004 cannot be spoofed by an adopter modifying their rule_id because the conflict-gate and Rego evaluation use the canonical rule_id from the finding's own record (set by scp_r_004_rule_id in the Rego). The warn-baseline rendering is keyed on the rule_id field in the deny output — there is no path by which a non-SCP-R-004 deny migrates into the warn branch unless the SCP source explicitly adds it to WARN_BASELINE_RULES. No new bypass surface introduced.
